title: From Awakening to Building: Liberal Arts "Next Moves" for Teaching and Learning in the Age of AI
author: AI Edu Simplified
summary: This article is a transcript of a keynote address at the University of Mary Washington's Liberal Arts in the Age of AI conference. The author uses Roland Barthes's analysis of wrestling — refusing to dismiss it as fake and instead reading it as a system for making meaning — as a frame for how educators should approach AI. The operating assumptions are that everyone is a critical thinker and that every generation's proclamation that young people are intellectually diminished has been wrong without exception. The 'next moves' framing argues that higher education must move from the awakening phase (recognizing AI exists) to the building phase: constructing curriculum, assignments, and practices that make genuine on what liberal arts education has always claimed to offer. AI clarifies rather than threatens the liberal arts mission.
points: Every generational claim that young people can no longer read, think, or reason has been wrong — the pattern of catastrophism about students repeats and fails every time.
Barthes's approach to wrestling — refusing to dismiss what others consider beneath them and instead reading it as a system for making meaning — models how educators should engage with AI.
Higher education has spent four years in the awakening phase; the next move is building — constructing curriculum and practices that deliver on what liberal arts has always promised.
The liberal arts mission — developing judgment, ethical reasoning, communication, and meaning-making — is clarified by AI, not threatened by it.
The question is not whether to adopt or resist AI but how to build learning experiences that help people become more fully themselves.
quotes: I categorically reject any discourse that begins from the position that people are somehow less than they were in the past.
Every generation, somebody stands up and announces that the young people have finally, this time, broken the covenant. And in every generation, that person is wrong. Not partly wrong. Wrong.
Wrestling is not a contest to be judged real or fake. It's a spectacle and it's a system for making meaning.
AI does not threaten the liberal arts mission. It clarifies it, stripping away false certainties and revealing the core.
The next moves are not about adopting AI or resisting AI. They are about building — building curriculum, assignments, and communities of practice that actually do what we have always claimed to do.
